title: Social Defeat Stress (SDS) in Mice: Using Swiss Mice as Resident
author: Marco Oreste F. Pagliusi Jr.
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Materials and Reagents Cleaning wipes At least 40 Swiss mice C57BL/6J mouse Wood chip bedding Alcohol 40% (storage at room temperature)

steps.title: Screen Swiss aggressors
steps.instruction: Purchase at least 40 retired‑breeder Swiss mice (6–12 months old) and single‑house them for one week with ad libitum food and water. Ten days before the first defeat session, screen each Swiss mouse in its home cage (wood‑chip bedding) by placing a C57BL/6J “screener” mouse inside for exactly 3 min. Record the latency to the first attack (seconds) and the total number of attacks using a mechanical tally counter. Stop the trial early if the Swiss mouse delivers >20 attacks; this day the Swiss mouse is a good aggressor. If the screener mouse obtains an open wound >1 cm, euthanize it immediately. Use the same screener mouse for up to five different Swiss mice per day; therefore at least eight screener mice are needed for 40 Swiss. Repeat the entire screening on two additional days (three days total), using a different screener mouse for each Swiss each day so that no Swiss meets the same screener twice.

substeps.instruction: Place Swiss mouse in its home cage with wood‑chip bedding.
Introduce a C57BL/6J screener mouse for 3 min.
Measure latency (<1 min) and count attacks.
Stop early if >20 attacks; otherwise continue full 3 min.
Remove screener mouse; repeat with next Swiss.
Use a new screener mouse after five uses.

steps.title: Select and house residents
steps.instruction: Identify Swiss mice that attacked the screener on at least two consecutive screening days with a latency <1 min. Discard any that do not meet this criterion. Rank the qualifying Swiss by total number of attacks over the three days and select the top performers as “residents” for the defeat protocol; keep the remaining qualified mice as reserve residents. Single‑house all selected residents (and reserves) with ad libitum food and water.

steps.title: Assemble defeat cages
steps.instruction: Set up laboratory‑rat breeding cages (minimum 10 cages, depending on the number of residents) by installing a perforated acrylic divider that allows sensory contact but prevents physical crossing. Provide free access to food and water on both sides and use wood‑chip bedding throughout. Designate the left compartment for the resident Swiss mouse and the right compartment for the C57BL/6J intruder.

steps.title: Habituate residents in cages
steps.instruction: Place each selected resident Swiss mouse on the left side of its defeat cage and allow a 2‑day habituation period before the first defeat session.

steps.title: Perform daily social defeat
steps.instruction: For each of 10 consecutive days, conduct a 10‑min agonistic encounter followed by separation and rotation:

substeps.instruction: Place one C57BL/6J mouse on the left side of the same defeat cage as its resident Swiss.
Allow 10 min of unrestricted interaction (social defeat).
After 10 min, move the C57BL/6J mouse to the right side of the cage, behind the perforated divider, maintaining sensory contact but preventing further physical attacks.

On the next day, line all defeat cages side‑by‑side on a bench. Transfer the C57BL/6J mouse from cage 1 to the left side of cage 2, from cage 2 to cage 3, …, and from the last cage to the left side of cage 1 (rotation).
Repeat the 10‑min interaction and separation for the rotated mice.

For control C57BL/6J mice, pair each with another control mouse behind a perforated divider for the entire 10‑day period, rotating pairs daily so that no two controls are together on consecutive days.

steps.title: End defeat and single‑house
steps.instruction: On the final (day 10) defeat session, after the 10‑min interaction separate the C57BL/6J mice and place each directly into an individual standard mouse cage with ad libitum food and water (single‑housing). The following day proceed to the social interaction test.

steps.title: Prepare interaction arena
steps.instruction: Position the social‑interaction arena under the video‑tracking system so the entire arena is captured from above. Clean the arena and the perforated acrylic enclosure with 40 % ethanol (room temperature) using cleaning wipes. Ensure the arena floor is white and define the interaction zone and corner zones in the tracking software as shown in Figure 3. Place an empty perforated acrylic enclosure in the center of the interaction zone.

steps.title: Run no‑target trial
steps.instruction: Place the test C57BL/6J mouse in the rear part of the arena opposite the interaction zone and record its behavior for 150 s. This is the “no‑target” trial because the enclosure is empty.

steps.title: Run target trial
steps.instruction: Return the C57BL/6J mouse to its home cage. Insert an unfamiliar aggressive Swiss mouse (reserve) into the perforated enclosure. After a 30‑s pause, place the same C57BL/6J mouse back in the rear part of the arena opposite the interaction zone and record for 150 s. This is the “target” trial.

steps.title: Clean arena and repeat
steps.instruction: After each mouse’s trials, remove both animals, clean the arena and the perforated enclosure again with 40 % ethanol, and repeat Steps C2‑C6 for all C57BL/6J mice, including control mice.
